Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the NovaVolt Motors Q3 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers’ presentation, there will be a question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one on your touchtone phone. To withdraw your question, press star then two. Today's conference call is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Chen, VP of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you, operator, and good morning, everyone. Welcome to NovaVolt Motors' Q3 2024 earnings call. Joining me today are Dr. Elena Vasquez, CEO; Michael Thornton, CFO; Raj Patel, Chief Manufacturing Officer; and other members of our leadership team.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that today's discussion may contain forward-looking statements that are subject to risks and uncertainties. Actual results may differ materially from those expressed or implied by these statements. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Vasquez.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, Sarah, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. Q3 was a strong quarter for NovaVolt Motors. We made significant progress in several key areas, including raw material sourcing and cost management, delivery volume guidance by model, total revenue and year-over-year growth, the impact of pricing strategies and promotional activities, and capital expenditure plans and investment priorities. The demand for our Apex series vehicles continues to be strong, and we are working diligently to increase production capacity to meet that demand. The impact of our premium platforms is exceeding our initial expectations.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael to discuss our financial performance in more detail.

Michael Thornton:
Thank you, Elena, and good morning, everyone. Good afternoon, actually, depending on your time zone. As we dive into our Q3 results, which underscore the accelerating momentum in our EV ecosystem amid a dynamic global market, let's start with the top line. For the quarter ended September 30, 2024, NovaVolt reported total revenue of $7.85 billion, marking a robust 51% year-over-year increase from $5.21 billion in Q3 2023. This performance not only exceeded our guidance midpoint but also surpassed consensus estimates by 8%, reflecting the strength of our vertical integration strategy—from cell-to-pack battery production to our proprietary 800-volt architecture—and our ability to capitalize on surging global EV demand.

Breaking it down by segment: Automotive revenue, which comprised 87% of the total at $6.83 billion, grew 58% year-over-year. This was driven by record vehicle deliveries of 185,000 units, up 62% from 114,000 units last year. Average selling price, or ASP, held steady at approximately $68,000 per vehicle, supported by a favorable product mix shift toward our premium models. The NovaVolt Apex SUV, our flagship with 500+ miles of EPA range on our next-gen NMC 2.0 cathodes, accounted for 42% of deliveries and delivered an ASP premium of 25% over our fleet average. We also saw meaningful contributions from regulatory credits, which added $420 million—up 35% year-over-year—as legacy automakers like GM and Ford ramp up their own EV transitions under tightening CAFE standards and EU CO2 regulations.

Energy generation and storage revenue hit $720 million, a stellar 112% year-over-year surge. Shipments of our Megapack 3.0 units—now boasting 4-hour duration with our LFP-silicon blend cells—reached 2.8 GWh, fueled by hyperscaler demand from the likes of Google and Microsoft for AI data center backup. This segment's gross margins expanded to 28%, benefiting from our Nevada Gigafactory ramp, where we're now producing at 95% of nameplate capacity. Services and other revenue contributed $300 million, up 22% year-over-year, driven by our growing Supercharge network, now with 18,000 stalls globally, and FSD subscription uptake at 65% of our eligible fleet.

Regionally, our performance was well-balanced but highlighted key growth vectors. In North America, which represented 62% of automotive revenue, we delivered 115,000 units—a 70% year-over-year increase—bolstered by the IRA's $7,500 point-of-sale incentives and our price adjustments earlier this year. Market share in the U.S. premium EV segment climbed to 28%, edging out Tesla's Model Y in Q3 registrations per Cox Automotive data. Europe contributed 22% of revenue with 41,000 deliveries, up 45% year-over-year, despite softer overall BEV sales amid subsidy phase-outs in Germany. Our localized production at the Berlin Gigafactory, now at 150,000 annual run-rate, mitigated tariffs and positioned us strongly against VW's ID.7 and BMW's i4. China remained a high-growth story at 12% of revenue, with 28,000 units delivered—up 110% year-over-year—thanks to our Shanghai plant's expansion and competitive pricing on the NovaVolt Pulse sedan, which undercuts BYD's Qin Plus EV by 10% while matching its 600 km CLTC range. We're gaining share in the mass-market segment, now at 4.2% per CAAM data, amid intensifying competition from Xiaomi's SU7.

These results validate our focus on supply chain resilience, tech leadership, and global scale. On the first, our in-house 4680 cell production hit 50 GWh annualized run-rate, reducing reliance on external suppliers like Panasonic by 40% and shielding us from lithium price volatility—spot carbonate prices fell 25% quarter-over-quarter but remain 60% below 2022 peaks. Technically, we're advancing our solid-state battery roadmap, with A-sample validation complete; pilot production starts Q1 2025, targeting 20% energy density gains over current LFP packs. This will underpin our $25,000 compact EV launch in H2 2026, aimed at volume leadership akin to Tesla's Model 2 ambitions.

Before moving on, I want to spend some time on raw material sourcing and cost management—a critical pillar of our profitability in this hyper-competitive EV landscape. With battery cell costs now representing roughly 35-40% of our vehicle bill of materials, mastering this area has been key to delivering our industry-leading gross margins of 28.2% this quarter, up 450 basis points year-over-year.

The raw materials market for EVs remains volatile but is showing signs of stabilization. Lithium carbonate prices, which peaked at over $80,000 per metric ton in late 2022, have corrected sharply to around $12,000-$15,000 per ton today—a roughly 80% decline—thanks to ramped-up supply from Australia and South America. Nickel, critical for our high-energy-density NMC cathodes, has fluctuated between $16,000-$20,000 per ton on the LME, influenced by Indonesian oversupply and the shift toward LFP chemistries. Cobalt prices have held steady at $25,000-$30,000 per ton amid ethical sourcing pressures, while graphite anode material from China continues to pressure margins at $500-$700 per ton.

Regionally, China's dominance—controlling 70% of global battery-grade refined lithium and over 90% of cathode precursors—poses risks, but it's also an opportunity. Our dual-sourcing strategy has reduced China exposure from 65% of our battery materials in 2022 to under 40% today, aligning with IRA localization incentives in the US and EU's Critical Raw Materials Act.

Turning to our execution: We've locked in 70% of our 2024-2026 lithium and nickel needs via long-term offtake agreements. For instance, our expanded deal with Albemarle at the Greenbushes mine in Australia secures 50,000 tons of spodumene concentrate annually at a blended price 15% below spot, with built-in escalators tied to production efficiencies. Similarly, we've partnered with Talon Metals in Minnesota for domestic nickel sulfate, qualifying for the full $7,500 IRA cathode credit per vehicle on our NovaVolt Prime SUV lineup.

Cost management initiatives are yielding tangible results. Our vertical integration playbook is accelerating: We've ramped our in-house cathode precursor plant in Nevada to 20 GWh capacity, cutting NMC 811 material costs by 22% through proprietary high-voltage doping processes that reduce nickel content by 5% while maintaining 250 Wh/kg density. On the LFP front—now 45% of our cell mix, up from 25% last year—we've qualified sodium-iron variants from our joint venture with CATL, slashing LFP cell costs to $52 per kWh, a 18% improvement quarter-over-quarter.

Recycling is a game-changer for sustainability and margins. Our Redwood Materials-inspired closed-loop program recovered 95% of black mass from end-of-life packs this quarter, yielding recycled nickel and lithium at 30-40% below virgin material costs. This fed directly into our Q3 COGS reduction of 12% per vehicle, with raw materials dropping from 42% to 38% of total COGS.

Strategically, we're hedging aggressively: 60% of exposed nickel and aluminum volumes are covered via LME futures, mitigating a potential $200 million P&L swing from last year's 25% price spike. We're also piloting solid-state electrolytes with our Samsung SDI collaboration, targeting a 15% BOM reduction by 2026 through lithium-metal anodes that cut cathode loading by 20%.

Looking forward, we expect battery material inflation to run at just 2-3% in FY24, versus the 15% we guided last year, driven by oversupply and our initiatives. This supports our raised FY24 gross margin guidance to 27-29%, with ASPs holding firm on premium platforms like the NovaVolt Apex sedan. Risks remain—geopolitical tensions in the DRC could lift cobalt 10-15%, and Red Sea disruptions have added 5% to Asian freight—but our diversified footprint positions us resiliently.

In summary, disciplined sourcing and cost levers have unlocked $450 million in savings year-to-date, fueling 25% EPS growth. We're not just managing costs; we're engineering a structural advantage in the EV race.

Shifting to the impact of our pricing strategies and promotional activities, which have been a key driver this quarter in a fiercely competitive EV market. Tesla's aggressive price cuts have set the pace globally, BYD is dominating in China with sub-$10,000 models, and legacy OEMs like Ford and GM are ramping up incentives on their Mustang Mach-E and Equinox EV platforms. Our approach has been deliberate—prioritizing volume growth and market share expansion while safeguarding long-term profitability through targeted cost discipline and tech-led differentiation.

In Q3, we delivered 68,000 vehicles globally, up from prior periods, fueled by adjustments in our fleet-average ASP. These moves directly addressed softening demand amid high interest rates and subsidy uncertainties. We leveraged our real-time analytics platform—powered by our in-house AI demand forecasting model—to adjust MSRPs regionally. In the U.S., where inventory levels improved, we optimized pricing on our core Apex X crossover, boosting conversion rates significantly. This elastic response showed strong price sensitivity.

Promotional activities amplified this. We deployed targeted incentives, achieving strong ROI based on incremental lifetime value. Key programs included U.S.-focused IRA-maximizing rebates stacking with federal credits for effective pricing under key thresholds, driving surges in U.S. volume and flipping market share in key segments against competitors like the Hyundai Ioniq 5. Leasing programs with low APRs accounted for a growing portion of volume, with residual values holding firm. In China, trade-in bonuses and free battery warranties stemmed share erosion amid intense competition from BYD's Seagull.

Regionally, North America saw improved inventory turns, clearing overhangs, though gross margins compressed from ASP dilution, offset by COGS reductions via scaled cell production. Europe required milder cuts and cash-back promos amid subsidy phase-outs, gaining share in premium segments. China saw ASP declines but cushioned margins through localization.

Financially, volume outpaced ASP declines, delivering net-positive results. Gross profit per unit adjusted, but total GM held with support from credits and other growth. This positions us for price normalization, with break-even ASPs improved via gigacasting and architecture efficiencies. Ahead, we embed incremental promo spend for growth, emphasizing tech premiumization, supply fortification, and regional tailoring like fleet deals and affordable variants.

Now, turning to delivery volume guidance by model for Q4 2024 and FY2025, reflecting our execution on the production ramp at GigaTexas and Fremont expansion. We've navigated softening demand in Europe due to subsidy phase-outs and competition from low-cost Chinese models like BYD's Seagull and Qin Plus EV. Our premium, tech-forward platforms—bolstered by 4680 cells and ApexDrive packs—position us for margin expansion.

Overall, Q4 2024 deliveries guided at 85,000 to 95,000 units, 25-35% sequential growth from Q3's 68,000 and 40-55% YoY. FY2024 full-year at 320,000 units, 60% over FY2023's 200,000, with energy storage offsetting softer ASPs.

FY2025 targets 450,000 to 500,000 units, 40-55% YoY, embedding conservative IRA, supply, and tariff assumptions.

By model: Apex X Crossover, core driver at 55% FY2025 mix. Q4: 50,000-55,000 units. FY2025: 250,000-275,000. North America 65% mix with fleet wins; Europe 25% localizing for subsidies; China/APAC 10%. Prioritizing for U.S. share capture, FSD take rates.

Apex T Pickup, high-margin at 25% mix. Q4: 20,000-25,000. FY2025: 110,000-125,000, mostly North America challenging Rivian/Ford, structural packs reducing costs.

Apex S Sedan, premium halo 15% mix. Q4: 10,000-12,000. FY2025: 65,000-75,000 globally, autonomy edge.

Apex A Compact, entry 5% mix. Q4 pilot 5,000; FY2025: 20,000-25,000 for IRA compliance.

Risks: consumer sentiment, yields. Upside: Robotaxi, credits, Mexico plant.

Our gross margin was 28.2%, reflecting ongoing efficiency. Operating expenses were $1.2 billion, net income $850 million. We maintain $12 billion in cash and equivalents. Guidance for Q4 is total revenue $8.4 to $8.8 billion.

As we wrap up, let's touch on capital expenditure plans and investment priorities, the linchpin to scale into a Tier 1 EV powerhouse. For FY2024, $9.8 billion deployed through Q3, on track for $12.5 billion, 22% up YoY, funded 65% from operations.

FY2025 capex $15.2-16.8 billion, midpoint $16 billion, assuming EV penetration growth and cost moderation. IRR at 15% min.

Priorities: 45% manufacturing expansion (~$7.2B)—Spartanburg Gigafactory South $2.5B for IRA credits, Berlin-adjacent $1.6B, Thailand JV $1.1B.

30% battery tech (~$4.8B)—Nevada CellForge to 100 GWh, upstream stakes, LFP pivot, solid-state R&D.

15% autonomy/software (~$2.4B)—compute to 10 exaFLOPS, sensors for Level 4.

10% charging (~$1.6B)—5,000 fast chargers.

North America 55%, Europe 25%, APAC 20%. Delivers capacity growth, cost reductions, share gains. Liquidity mitigates risks.

I'll now turn the call over to Raj to provide an update on our manufacturing operations.

Raj Patel:
Thank you, Michael. We are pleased with the progress we've made in scaling up production of the Apex series. Production lines at Fremont and GigaTexas are hitting high utilization, with OEE at 95% on key models, thanks to initiatives like Gen 3 heat pumps and structural battery packs v2. We're implementing several programs to further improve efficiency, such as gigacasting for body-in-white and unibody skateboard sharing parts across models, reducing costs 40%. We're on track to meet our production targets for the year, with 50 GWh cell output and expansions supporting FY2025 volumes.

Now, I'll hand the call back to the operator for the Q&A session.

Operator:
Thank you. We will now begin the question and answer session. If you would like to ask a question, please press star then one. Our first question comes from John Miller with Goldman Sachs.

Analyst 1:
Thanks, and congrats on a strong quarter. On raw materials, with lithium stabilizing but cobalt risks from DRC, how much buffer do your hedges provide if prices spike 15%? And any updates on solid-state pilots?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thanks, John. Our 60% hedge coverage on nickel and aluminum via LME futures already mitigated last year's swings, and for cobalt, diversified sourcing keeps exposure low. The Samsung SDI solid-state pilots are advancing, targeting 15% BOM cuts by 2026—early data shows promise on lithium-metal anodes. We're confident in resilience.

Operator:
Next question from Lisa Chen at Morgan Stanley.

Analyst 2:
Great, thanks. On delivery guidance, the Apex T pickup ramp sounds aggressive at 150% YoY. What gives you confidence on supply for the truck line, especially with 4680 yields?

Michael Thornton:
Lisa, the Texas line is at 1,000/week run rate, resolving prior tooling delays. Panasonic yields are above 85%, and our structural pack v2 cuts BoM 20% to $120/kWh. Fleet demand and Cybertruck conversions add tailwinds—90% North America mix de-risks it.

Operator:
Our next question from David Ruiz with JPMorgan.

Analyst 3:
Thanks. Raj, on manufacturing, with Fremont at 95% OEE, any bottlenecks in Apex A compact pilot? And how does Berlin ramp factor into Europe volumes?

Raj Patel:
David, Apex A pilot is smooth on LFP lines, CATL cells at $85/kWh enabling affordability. Berlin Gigafactory starts Q1'25 at 150k run-rate, qualifying for BAFA subsidies and countering VW price wars—15% efficiency edge secures premium share.

Operator:
Next from Emma Patel at Barclays.

Analyst 4:
Thanks. Michael, pricing promos ate into margins—any quantification on Q4 spend, and how tech bundles like FSD lift ASPs?

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Emma, Q4 embeds $50-100M incremental promos for 20% YoY growth, but Level 3 autonomy trials at no extra cost target 35% attach, +$2k ASP. Break-even at $38k on Apex X via efficiencies. It's volume for long-term scale.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for your questions. We have time for one more.

Operator:
Our final question from Tom Bradley at UBS.

Analyst 5:
Congrats team. On capex, Spartanburg DOE loans—timeline? And LFP pivot details for NovaCompact versus BYD?

Michael Thornton:
Tom, $1.2B DOE loans close Q1'25, ramping Spartanburg to 500k units H2'25 for $450M annual IRA credits. NovaCompact LFP at 40% new capacity matches Seagull pricing, U.S. assembly for bonuses—sub-$30k leasing.

Operator:
Thank you. I would now like to turn the call back to Dr. Vasquez for closing remarks.

Dr. Elena Vasquez:
Thank you, operator, and thank you all for joining us today. We are confident in our ability to continue executing our strategy and delivering value to our shareholders. We look forward to updating you on our progress next quarter.

Sarah Chen:
Thank you for joining us today. This concludes the NovaVolt Motors Q3 2024 earnings call. You may now disconnect.
